title: Per-request KPI handoff router with adaptive sampling
creator: Aisha Varma
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight per-request KPIs handoff router that accepts OTLP/Prometheus micro-batches from inference sidecars and routes/normalizes them into the central metric fabric with tenant-aware adaptive sampling. The router should preserve SLI fidelity for latency and error dashboards while reducing cardinality and ingestion costs under high multi-tenant load.

Scope and deliverables:
- Ingest OTLP metric points and Prometheus pushgateway-style envelopes from sidecars and edge proxies. Support batch and streaming (gRPC/HTTP) paths.
- Implement adaptive sampling rules: tenant hot-spot detection, per-route importance scoring, and exemplar selection for traces. Sampling modes: preserve-errors, latency-tail-preserve, token-cost-priority, and background-sampling.
- Normalize labels to canonical schema: model, model_variant, route, tenant_id, request_size_tokens, cpu_class, region. Emit mapping metrics for downstream rollups.
- Emit histogram metrics with stable buckets for llm_request_duration_seconds and inference_token_count; attach deterministic exemplars for 99th/99.9th percentile linking to traces.
- Backpressure and dead-letter strategy: local buffer with exponential backoff to central fan-in; fail-open to minimally aggregated rollup if central gateway unavailable. Provide replayable DLQ in S3 for reprocessing.
- Admin controls in Console: per-tenant sampling thresholds, blacklist/whitelist routes, and a trial canary toggle.

Architecture notes and trade-offs:
- We chose an inline router (small stateless service) rather than a heavy edge aggregator to reduce operational coupling and simplify rollouts. This increases per-request network hops but keeps compute isolated from sidecars.
- Adaptive sampling uses a lightweight in-memory sketch for tenant hot detection to avoid per-tenant state explosion; sketch parameters are tunable via feature flags. This sacrifices exactness for bounded memory and predictable CPU.
- Exemplars are deterministically sampled using a hash of request_id to provide reproducible trace links across retries. This keeps trace linking deterministic but reduces randomness benefits for low-volume tenants.

SLOs and success criteria:
- No more than 2% regression in dashboard 99th latency compared to current production baseline after sampling enabled (per-route adjustable).
- Reduce ingestion cardinality by 40-70% for noisy tenants under load in the adaptive sampling experiments.
- End-to-end added request latency <= 0.8ms median and <= 3ms P99 in the routing path.

Integration and rollout plan:
1) Deploy router as a managed sidecar-enabled service to staging and run canary with 10% of traffic.
2) Validate exemplar->trace linking with existing tracing hooks (ENG-61234 & ENG-67108).
3) Ramp tenant sampling policies and monitor cost signals in Console.
4) Full rollout with opt-out for high-compliance tenants.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Per-Request+KPI+Handoff+Router
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/942
- Benchmark dashboard (Grafana): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/telemetry/llm-kpi-router-canary

Open questions / TODOs:
- Finalize exemplar format to ensure compatibility with Prometheus exemplars and OTLP attributes.
- Decide retention policy for replay DLQ (30 vs 90 days).
- Confirm integration pattern with tenant RBAC for private deployments (affects encryption of DLQ and admin controls).
